text: I know you don't mean this negatively but I feel as though you should know from someone around the same age as Boa that comments like this sometimes feel a bit like a back handed compliment. Although it is meant positively, the underlying assumption is quite ageist. It puts pressure on women to look young. It reinforces the societal standard that looking old is a negative thing, despite the fact that it is a very natural human process. If Boa had wrinkles and grey hair, it would not change her ability nor her artistry but it would change how people view her and that is very disheartening. Instead of saying 'you look so young', just say 'you look beautiful'. No one looks young forever so putting that pressure on someone to maintain their youth is an unrealistic expectation and so harmful for someone's self esteem when they do start to develop visible 'signs of age'. Beauty should not be defined by age and age should not define you.
